assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers turned a chemically simple, solution-processable material class into photovoltaics rising from a few percent to above 25 percent efficiency within a decade. The impact on energy conversion, defect chemistry and materials design is large, original and clearly chemical, with a very clear first demonstration and rapid independent reproduction.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cells; Park and Grätzel (with Snaith and Seok in the independent line) made the solid-state, stable device; Snaith's meso-superstructured and planar cells opened the thin-film route. Credit is spread over more than three people, so any trio leaves out Grätzel, Seok, Kanatzidis and others. My recollection is that Kojima is not on the supplied list; I cannot verify that.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by thousands of groups; efficiency records are independently certified. Timing is ripe, though long-term stability and commercialization are not yet settled.
uncertainties: Which three of Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel and Seok best represent the decisive contributions is contested.
Operational stability and manufacturing maturity remain open, which could argue that recognition is slightly early.
Whether the supplied names omit an early originator I cannot confirm.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is the physical-chemical principle behind respiratory enzymes, photosynthesis and many catalytic cycles. A unified theory and model-compound work that separates concerted from stepwise pathways is a conceptual contribution of lasting value to the mechanisms of biological energy conversion, which I know well.
assessment.attribution: Meyer established early PCET concepts and molecular electrocatalysis; Mayer defined bond-dissociation free-energy thermodynamics and concerted PCET kinetics; Hammes-Schiffer provided the theoretical framework. Nocera is strong for solar fuels and PCET in proteins but his decisive contribution is partly in another discovery. The three chosen give a coherent concept-theory-experiment configuration.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are widely adopted and tested in enzymes, molecular catalysts and electrode interfaces. The field is mature, and a single decisive experiment is less obvious than a unifying framework.
uncertainties: The discovery is a framework rather than one landmark observation, which makes the prize motivation harder to write.
Overlap with Nocera's artificial photosynthesis work and with Marcus-type theory already recognized.
Relative weight of experiment versus theory in credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation through PROTACs and molecular glues introduces a new mechanistic mode of drug action, event-driven rather than occupancy-driven. The concept is original, chemically driven and now supported by clinical-stage compounds. It also links to the mechanism of thalidomide-like drugs.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies authored the first PROTAC concept and demonstration; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, underlying molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray also have significant contributions, so choosing three is difficult. Crews, Deshaies and Handa cover PROTAC concept and degrader mechanism.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation in many labs and numerous clinical trials. Clinical approval of a PROTAC is not yet reached, so some members may think recognition is premature.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is incomplete; therapeutic payoff still pending.
The separate PROTAC and molecular-glue histories may need different recognition.
Several credible contributors (Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto) would be left out.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing transformed biology and medicine, with chemistry at its core: reversible terminator chemistry, clonal amplification and pyrosequencing-type detection. Impact is outstanding and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the Solexa chemistry; Rothberg commercialised semiconductor and 454 pyrosequencing technology. Mayer and Ju contributed relevant but different approaches. Industrial and technological credit is intertwined, and the field was built by several parallel technologies.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with universal use for two decades; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: A prize may be seen as more biology or technology than chemistry.
Industrial versus academic credit and the plurality of platforms complicate attribution.
Parallel development by 454 and Solexa means a three-person selection is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel view of protein folding resolved Levinthal's paradox in physical terms and linked statistical mechanics to kinetic experiments. Its importance for biophysical chemistry is high, and the conceptual originality is clear to me as a physics-trained biophysicist.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson) developed the theory; Fersht's protein-engineering and phi-value analysis gave decisive experimental mapping; Dill's hydrophobic-collapse models were an influential alternative view. Three names leave out Bryngelson and Dill.
assessment.maturity: The concepts are deeply embedded in the field. Recent structure-prediction advances were recognised in 2024, which shifts the context but does not remove the fundamental physics.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize on protein structure prediction and design could reduce appetite.
Theory and experiment credit are hard to split and the field's early history is multi-authored.
Some members may regard the funnel as a conceptual picture more than a discrete discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one DNA base into another without double-strand breaks, a protein-evolution and nucleoside-chemistry achievement with large therapeutic implications. Original and rapidly consequential.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conception and development of cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were lead authors of the key papers, while Nishida and Kondo reported an independent cytidine deaminase fusion. A prize for Liu alone sidesteps trainee credit, though possible adjacency to CRISPR laureates and to prime editing is not resolved.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is extensive and clinical use has begun, but long-term outcomes are still developing; timing is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Fit as chemistry rather than medicine or genetics.
Early clinical data only; maturity is moderate.
Relation to prime editing (a separate candidate with partly overlapping people) may change how to frame the prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental demonstration of long-range electron tunnelling in proteins, using ruthenium-modified metalloproteins, gave quantitative distance and driving-force dependence and a tunnelling-pathways picture. It underpins our understanding of respiratory and photosynthetic electron transfer, which is close to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Gray is the central figure and Winkler the long-standing collaborator; Beratan, Onuchic and Moser-Dutton also contributed to the theory and empirical rules and are not on the list. A two-person prize is possible but excludes theory contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature, well confirmed and textbook knowledge for decades. Some members may regard Marcus's 1992 prize as having covered the main idea.
uncertainties: Overlap with the prior Marcus recognition.
Winkler's role relative to the theory contributors who are not in the supplied credits.
Perceived age of the work may reduce urgency.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle for cellular compartments has changed how cell biology and biophysical chemistry think of intracellular organisation. The originality is high and the physical-chemical concepts are clear.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behave as liquids; Rosen showed multivalent-interaction-driven phase transitions. Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded physical principles. Credit is shared across several people.
assessment.maturity: Fast-growing field with many confirmations, but debate remains about which condensates are functionally phase-separated in vivo; maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Controversy over physiological relevance and over whether many reported condensates are artefacts of overexpression.
Biology versus chemistry fit.
Difficult selection among five credible contributors.
